_meta.description: Verified catalog of node-runtime upgrade breakers (Step 2 of the Upgrade Breakage Radar backfill). Consumed by NodeRuntimeCatalog for NodeRuntimeAnalyzer. Covers facts about the NODE itself (container runtime, host cgroup version) rather than API schema, config fields, or CLI flags — the other three catalogs' domain.
_meta.verificationMethod: Every removedInVersion/appliesFromVersion value below was read directly from the official kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-<version>.md files, or (for containerRuntimeVersion / cgroup-version-observability) the upstream Go source (k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go NodeSystemInfo, k8s.io/kubelet/config/v1beta1/types.go KubeletConfiguration). Exact source URL + matched sentence is recorded per-entry below in `provenance`. NONE of these values were hand-typed from memory.
_meta.honestyNote: detectable=true means the underlying Kubernetes API genuinely exposes the fact needed (verified against upstream Go source) — it does NOT mean OUR agent currently collects it. NodeRuntimeAnalyzer independently determines, per-cluster and per-run, whether the currently-synced node inventory actually carries the needed field; if not, it emits a distinct NOT-ASSESSED finding rather than a false 'clean'. detectable=false (cgroupVersion) means NO Kubernetes API surface exposes the fact AT ALL, under any collector — this is permanently advisory, never a 'detected' finding.
_meta.coveredThroughVersion: 1.16-1.37 (Step 3, 2026-07-11, extended the 1.24/1.35 Step 2 starter pair back across the 1.16-1.31 backfill range)
_meta.step3Note: Step 3 (2026-07-11) added 6 new PERMANENTLY-non-detectable node-runtime rules (dockershim-adjacent kubelet CLI flags removed at 1.24; CRI v1alpha2 dropped at 1.26; --container-runtime kubelet flag removed at 1.27; cgroup v1 support for the swap feature removed at 1.28 -- narrower/earlier than the existing 1.35 failCgroupV1 rule; kubelet hard-rejects AppArmor pods without host AppArmor support at 1.31; DRA v1alpha2 kubelet gRPC API unsupported at 1.31), all surfaced via the SAME generalized 'always advisory once target>=removedInVersion' analyzer path the original cgroup-v1-fails-1.35 rule used (NodeRuntimeAnalyzer's single-rule-ID special case was generalized into a loop over every detectable=false catalog rule). The 1.20 dockershim DEPRECATION-announcement item (PR #94624) was intentionally NOT added as a separate rule -- it predates and is fully superseded by the existing actionable rtz-k8s-node-dockershim-removed (1.24) rule; a 1.20 rule would fire as noise for every cluster upgrading past 1.20 with no additional action value. In-tree cloud-provider removals (1.29 default-off, 1.30 Azure/vSphere, 1.31 GCP) were intentionally routed to the ADVISORY catalog instead of here or config-breaker: they are really a `--cloud-provider=X` VALUE-specific fact, and neither this analyzer's Node-status surface nor ConfigBreakerAnalyzer's componentFlag 'present' condition can distinguish a specific flag VALUE (vs. e.g. --cloud-provider=external, which remains valid) -- modeling it here would risk a false positive at scale, so it is advisory-only per this backfill's no-false-precision guardrail. Total: 2 -> 8 rules.

rules.title: Node reports the Docker/dockershim container runtime, which was removed from the kubelet in Kubernetes 1.24
rules.remediation: Migrate this node to a full CRI-compliant container runtime (containerd, CRI-O, etc.) BEFORE upgrading kubelet to 1.24+ — dockershim was completely removed from the kubelet at 1.24 and the node will not be able to run Pods afterward.
rules.note: containerRuntimeVersion IS a real, stable, GA-guaranteed corev1.NodeSystemInfo field (json tag `containerRuntimeVersion`, doc comment: 'ContainerRuntime Version reported by the node through runtime remote API (e.g. containerd://1.4.2)') — VERIFIED against the live k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go source. However, as of this investigation (2026-07-11) the runtimez_agent's ResourceMapper.map(Node) does NOT project this field into the synced Node.status JSON (it currently emits only capacity/allocatable/kubeletVersion/osImage/ready) — see step2_summary.md for the full gap analysis. NodeRuntimeAnalyzer therefore checks for the field's actual presence per-cluster at runtime and reports NOT-ASSESSED (never a false 'clean') for every cluster until the agent is updated to project it.

provenance.name: kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-1.24.md
provenance.matchedText: Docker runtime support using dockershim in the kubelet is now completely removed in 1.24. The kubelet used to have a module called dockershim, which implements CRI support for Docker, and it has seen maintenance issues in the Kubernetes community. From 1.24 onwards, please move to a container runtime that is a full-fledged implementation of CRI (v1alpha1 or v1 compliant) as they become available. (#97252, @dims)

rules.title: ACTION REQUIRED (upstream): nodes running cgroup v1 will not start on kubelet 1.35+ by default (failCgroupV1)
rules.remediation: Verify each node's ACTUAL cgroup version manually before upgrading to 1.35+ (e.g. `stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup/` on the host — cgroup2fs means v2, tmpfs means v1). From Kubernetes 1.35, the kubelet's failCgroupV1 config option defaults to true and the kubelet refuses to start on a cgroup v1 host unless you explicitly set failCgroupV1:false (a stop-gap, not a fix — cgroup v1 is now deprecated). This platform CANNOT auto-detect the host's cgroup version — no Kubernetes API field exposes it.
rules.note: PERMANENTLY NOT DETECTABLE, not merely a current agent-collection gap: verified by inspecting BOTH k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go NodeSystemInfo (machineID/systemUUID/bootID/kernelVersion/osImage/containerRuntimeVersion/kubeletVersion/kubeProxyVersion/operatingSystem/architecture — no cgroup field of any kind) AND k8s.io/kubelet/config/v1beta1/types.go KubeletConfiguration (cgroupDriver/cgroupsPerQOS/cgroupRoot/failCgroupV1 are all CONFIGURATION knobs, none of them report the actual detected host cgroup version). The closest adjacent, genuinely detectable signal — whether a kubelet config has explicitly set failCgroupV1:false (i.e., deliberately disabled the safety net) — is modeled separately as a DETECTABLE ConfigBreakerCatalog rule (rtz-k8s-kubelet-fail-cgroup-v1-disabled); that rule detects the OVERRIDE, not the underlying cgroup-v1 fact itself. This rule is therefore always surfaced as an advisory the moment target>=1.35, independent of any collected data, and NEVER as a 'detected' finding.

rules.title: Dockershim-related kubelet CLI flags were removed alongside dockershim in Kubernetes 1.24
rules.remediation: Remove --experimental-dockershim-root-directory, --docker-endpoint, --image-pull-progress-deadline, --network-plugin, --cni-conf-dir, --cni-bin-dir, --cni-cache-dir, and --network-plugin-mtu from the kubelet's command line / systemd unit before upgrading to 1.24+ (same release as the dockershim removal itself, rtz-k8s-node-dockershim-removed). Verify manually -- NOT auto-detectable: these are kubelet BINARY-only CLI flags never exposed via /configz (confirmed absent from the current KubeletConfiguration v1beta1 struct) and the kubelet has no static-pod command[]/args[] representation.
rules.note: PERMANENTLY NOT DETECTABLE (same structural reason as the config-breaker catalog's kubelet-CLI-only entries): VERIFIED absent from k8s.io/kubelet/config/v1beta1/types.go (no networkPlugin/cniConfDir/cniBinDir/cniCacheDir/dockerEndpoint/dockershimRootDirectory/imagePullProgressDeadline fields in the current struct) and the kubelet is a host-level process with no Kubernetes Pod/static-pod representation. Always surfaced as an advisory the moment target>=1.24, independent of any collected node data.

rules.title: Container Runtime Interface (CRI) v1alpha2 support was dropped in Kubernetes 1.26 -- runtimes must implement CRI v1
rules.remediation: Verify every node's container runtime (containerd, CRI-O, etc.) implements the CRI v1 API before upgrading to 1.26+ -- very old runtime versions that only implement CRI v1alpha2 will fail to communicate with the kubelet. Verify manually -- NOT auto-detectable: no Kubernetes API field exposes which CRI protocol version a runtime implements (Node.status.nodeInfo.containerRuntimeVersion exposes the runtime NAME and VERSION string, e.g. 'containerd://1.4.2', but not the CRI protocol version it speaks); inferring this from runtime version numbers would require a hardcoded per-runtime version-threshold table not confirmed in the source changelog and is deliberately NOT modeled here to avoid inventing false precision.
rules.note: PERMANENTLY NOT DETECTABLE with today's data surfaces: verified against k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go NodeSystemInfo (containerRuntimeVersion is a free-text 'name://version' string, not a CRI protocol version). A per-runtime version-threshold heuristic (e.g. 'containerd < 1.4 only supports v1alpha2') was considered and REJECTED per this backfill's no-false-precision guardrail -- no such threshold is stated in the verified changelog text. Always surfaced as an advisory the moment target>=1.26.

provenance.name: kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-1.26.md
provenance.matchedText: Dropped support for the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) version `v1alpha2`, which means that container runtimes just have to implement `v1`. ([#110618](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110618), [@saschagrunert](https://github.com/saschagrunert)) [SIG Node and Security]

rules.title: kubelet flag --container-runtime was removed in Kubernetes 1.27
rules.remediation: Remove --container-runtime from the kubelet's command line / systemd unit before upgrading to 1.27+ (the flag was already a no-op after dockershim's 1.24 removal, since 'remote' was the only valid value; this is its final removal). Verify manually -- NOT auto-detectable: the kubelet is a host-level process with no static-pod command[]/args[] representation for this platform's collection surfaces to scan.
rules.note: PERMANENTLY NOT DETECTABLE: kubelet BINARY-only CLI flag, no static-pod representation, and not part of the typed KubeletConfiguration struct served by /configz. Always surfaced as an advisory the moment target>=1.27.

rules.title: cgroup v1 support for the swap-memory (NodeSwap) feature was removed in Kubernetes 1.28
rules.remediation: If this cluster uses the NodeSwap feature (swap memory for container workloads), verify every node's cgroup version manually before upgrading to 1.28+ -- cgroup v1 support was removed SPECIFICALLY for the swap feature at 1.28 (a narrower, earlier-and-scoped fact than the general failCgroupV1 kubelet-startup gate that arrives platform-wide at 1.35, see rtz-k8s-node-cgroupv1-fails-1.35). Clusters not using the NodeSwap feature are unaffected by this specific item. This platform CANNOT auto-detect a host's cgroup version -- no Kubernetes API field exposes it.
rules.note: PERMANENTLY NOT DETECTABLE, same structural reason as rtz-k8s-node-cgroupv1-fails-1.35 (no Kubernetes API surface exposes host cgroup version). Scoped MEDIUM (not HIGH/CRITICAL) because this specific 1.28 event only affects clusters that have opted into the NodeSwap feature gate on cgroup v1 hosts -- a narrower audience than the general 1.35 failCgroupV1 default-on event. Always surfaced as an advisory the moment target>=1.28, entirely independent of any collected node data.

provenance.name: kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-1.28.md
provenance.matchedText: Support for `cgroup v1` is removed. ([#118764](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118764), [@iholder101](https://github.com/iholder101)) [SIG Node and Testing] -- quoted in the context of the NodeSwap / swap-memory-for-containers feature note block (immediately preceded by: 'Containers with memory requests equal to their memory limits also won't have swap access...The formula for the swap limit for Burstable QoS pods is: (<memory-request>/<node-memory-capacity>)*<node-swap-capacity>.')

rules.title: kubelet hard-rejects Pods requesting AppArmor if the node does not have AppArmor enabled, from Kubernetes 1.31
rules.remediation: Verify every node in this cluster actually has AppArmor enabled (kernel LSM support + apparmor_parser installed) before upgrading to 1.31+ if any workloads request AppArmor profiles -- previously such Pods may have silently run unconfined on nodes without AppArmor; from 1.31 the kubelet now hard-rejects (fails to admit) these Pods instead. Verify manually -- NOT auto-detectable: no Kubernetes Node API field reports whether a host has AppArmor support/enabled.
rules.note: PERMANENTLY NOT DETECTABLE: verified against k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go NodeSystemInfo -- no AppArmor-related field exists (host security-module support is not part of the Node API in any form). Always surfaced as an advisory the moment target>=1.31.

provenance.matchedText: Kubelet now hard rejects pods with AppArmor if the node does not have AppArmor enabled. ([#125776](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125776), [@vinayakankugoyal](https://github.com/vinayakankugoyal)) [SIG Node]

rules.title: ACTION REQUIRED: DRA drivers using the v1alpha2 kubelet gRPC API are no longer supported from Kubernetes 1.31
rules.remediation: If this cluster uses Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), verify every DRA driver has been updated to the newer kubelet gRPC API before upgrading to 1.31+ -- drivers still using the v1alpha2 API will stop working. Verify manually -- NOT auto-detectable: no Kubernetes Node/resource-slice API field reports which gRPC API version a DRA driver plugin implements.
rules.note: PERMANENTLY NOT DETECTABLE with today's data surfaces: this is a driver-plugin-side gRPC protocol version, not a fact reported anywhere in the Node or DRA resource-slice API objects this platform collects. Always surfaced as an advisory the moment target>=1.31.
